Coastal towns brace for storm

By Jane Doe, BBC News

Thousands of homes are without power and rail services have been cancelled as a powerful storm sweeps across the west coast, forecasters have warned.

The Met Office issued an amber warning for wind, saying gusts of up to 90mph were possible in exposed areas until Monday morning.

Emergency shelters opened

Councils in three counties have opened emergency shelters, and residents in low-lying areas have been told to prepare to leave their homes.

Ferry operator Caledonian MacBrayne has suspended all sailings on its west coast routes, while dozens of flights have been grounded.

Advertisement

“Our crews are working through the night,” said a spokesman for the electricity network. “We expect to restore supplies to most homes by Sunday afternoon.”
